trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by BMP10 or FKTN? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison (canonical UniProt sequences):**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| BMP10 | O95393 (BMP10_HUMAN, precursor) | 530 aa | **60,350 Da ≈ 60.35 kDa** |
| FKTN | O75072 (FKTN_HUMAN, fukutin) | 461 aa | **53,724 Da ≈ 53.72 kDa** |

BMP10 is the heavier protein, by about 6.6 kDa.

Note: the BMP10 mass is for the full-length precursor; the mature secreted BMP10 chain (residues 317–424) is only ~12 kDa, which would be lighter than FKTN. Also, BMP10's annotated length (530 aa) is inconsistent with its chain ending at residue 424 plus propeptide — the entry's feature coordinates cover only the first 424 residues of a 530-residue sequence, which looks like an annotation gap.

trace.task_prompt: Does protein P50553 have more than 259 residues? Answer yes or no and give the count. Put exactly "yes" or "no" in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text:
I looked up P50553 (ASCL1_HUMAN, Achaete-scute homolog 1).

- The record's `sequence.length` is **283**, and manually counting the returned sequence string also gives 283 residues.
- 283 > 259 → **yes**.

Caveat: the annotation is internally inconsistent — the "Chain" feature (PRO_0000127126) spans residues 1–236, and the canonical human ASCL1 is normally 236 aa. The returned sequence carries an extra ~47-residue C-terminal segment (`...GCNCKRSGCLKNYCECYEAKIMCSSICKCIGCK`) that looks like a cysteine-rich CRC/tesmin-like motif, not ASCL1. If the true chain length of 236 is used instead, the answer would be "no". The stated molecular weight (30,632 Da) is consistent with the 283-residue sequence, not with a 236-residue one.

{"answer": "yes", "concerns": ["Record's sequence length (283) conflicts with the Chain feature annotation 1-236 and with the canonical 236-aa human ASCL1; the extra C-terminal ~47 residues (cysteine-rich CRC/tesmin-like motif) appear foreign to ASCL1", "If the 236-residue chain is taken as the protein length, the answer would flip to 'no'", "molWeight 30632 Da matches the 283-residue sequence, so the anomalous extension is part of the stored sequence rather than a display error"]}

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by AOAH or ZNF219? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Results**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Stated mol. weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| AOAH | P28039 (AOAH_HUMAN) | 719 aa (as returned) | 81,576 Da ≈ **81.6 kDa** |
| ZNF219 | Q9P2Y4 (ZN219_HUMAN) | 722 aa | 76,877 Da ≈ **76.9 kDa** |

**Important caveat:** the AOAH record is internally inconsistent. Every annotation in the entry stops at residue 575 — the precursor chain features ("small subunit" 35–156, "large subunit" 157–575), the last disulfide (376–459), the last glycosylation site (466), and the last PDB-derived secondary-structure element (helix 562–569 / turn 570–573). The canonical human AOAH precursor is 575 aa (~63 kDa). The returned sequence carries ~144 extra, highly Gly/Pro/Arg/Asp-rich residues after position 575 that are not covered by any feature and that inflate the reported mass by roughly 16–18 kDa.

- Taking the returned molWeight field at face value: AOAH (81.6 kDa) > ZNF219 (76.9 kDa).
- Taking the annotated 575-residue AOAH precursor (~63 kDa), which is what all the entry's evidence supports: **ZNF219 (76.9 kDa) is the heavier protein.**

I go with the annotation-consistent interpretation: ZNF219 ≈ 76.9 kDa is heavier than genuine AOAH (~63 kDa; 81.6 kDa as literally reported).

**Important caveat:** the AOAH record is internally inconsistent. Every annotation in the entry stops at residue 575 — the precursor chain features ("small subunit" 35–156, "large subunit" 157–575), the last disulfide (376–459), the last glycosylation site (466), and the last PDB-derived secondary-structure element (helix 562–569 / turn 570–573). The canonical human AOAH precursor is 575 aa (~63 kDa). The returned sequence carries ~144 extra, highly Gly/Pro/Arg/Asp-rich residues after position 575 that are not covered by any feature and that inflate the reported mass by roughly 16–18 kDa.

- Taking the returned molWeight field at face value: AOAH (81.6 kDa) > ZNF219 (76.9 kDa).
- Taking the annotated 575-residue AOAH precursor (~63 kDa), which is what all the entry's evidence supports: **ZNF219 (76.9 kDa) is the heavier protein.**

I go with the annotation-consistent interpretation: ZNF219 ≈ 76.9 kDa is heavier than genuine AOAH (~63 kDa; 81.6 kDa as literally reported).

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**FPGT — O14772** (Fucose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase)
- Canonical sequence: 607 aa, **68,010 Da ≈ 68.0 kDa**
- Record is internally consistent (chain 1–607 matches sequence length).

**PSIP1 — O75475** (PC4 and SFRS1-interacting protein / LEDGF p75)
- The record as returned reports 662 aa / 74,494 Da ≈ 74.5 kDa, **but this sequence appears corrupted**: the annotated chain is "PC4 and SFRS1-interacting protein, 1–530", all isoform/alternative-sequence features end at residue 530, and the extra 132 C‑terminal residues ("HLEHLSLAHNRLAM…LDLSCNS") are a leucine‑rich‑repeat–like stretch unrelated to the HDGF-family PSIP1 and absent from the real entry. Subtracting those 132 residues gives ≈ **60.1 kDa** for the genuine 530‑aa p75 protein (matching the documented UniProt value of 60,103 Da).

**Conclusion:** Using the true canonical PSIP1 chain (530 aa, ~60.1 kDa), **FPGT (~68.0 kDa) is the heavier protein**. Note that if one naively trusted the inflated 662‑aa PSIP1 sequence (74.5 kDa), the comparison would flip — so this answer depends on the flagged data problem.

**FPGT — O14772** (Fucose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase)
- Canonical sequence: 607 aa, **68,010 Da ≈ 68.0 kDa**
- Record is internally consistent (chain 1–607 matches sequence length).

**PSIP1 — O75475** (PC4 and SFRS1-interacting protein / LEDGF p75)
- The record as returned reports 662 aa / 74,494 Da ≈ 74.5 kDa, **but this sequence appears corrupted**: the annotated chain is "PC4 and SFRS1-interacting protein, 1–530", all isoform/alternative-sequence features end at residue 530, and the extra 132 C‑terminal residues ("HLEHLSLAHNRLAM…LDLSCNS") are a leucine‑rich‑repeat–like stretch unrelated to the HDGF-family PSIP1 and absent from the real entry. Subtracting those 132 residues gives ≈ **60.1 kDa** for the genuine 530‑aa p75 protein (matching the documented UniProt value of 60,103 Da).

**Conclusion:** Using the true canonical PSIP1 chain (530 aa, ~60.1 kDa), **FPGT (~68.0 kDa) is the heavier protein**. Note that if one naively trusted the inflated 662‑aa PSIP1 sequence (74.5 kDa), the comparison would flip — so this answer depends on the flagged data problem.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| CTDSPL2 | Q05D32 (CTD small phosphatase‑like protein 2) | 466 aa | 52,999 Da ≈ **53.0 kDa** |
| DPH1 | Q9BZG8 (2‑(3‑amino‑3‑carboxypropyl)histidine synthase subunit 1) | 548 aa | 61,196 Da ≈ **61.2 kDa** |

As annotated in UniProt, **DPH1 (~61.2 kDa) is heavier than CTDSPL2 (~53.0 kDa)**, a difference of ~8 kDa.

Caveat: the DPH1 entry's displayed sequence is 548 aa, yet its mature "Chain" feature is annotated only as residues 1–438 (and the C‑terminal ~110 residues look like an unrelated coiled‑coil segment, consistent with a read‑through/extended isoform). If only the 1–438 chain were counted (~48 kDa), the ranking would reverse — so the conclusion depends on using the full canonical sequence mass.

I retrieved P51795 (CLCN5_HUMAN, H(+)/Cl(-) exchange transporter 5).

- Reported sequence length: **1020** residues (molWeight 114,284); I manually re-counted the sequence string and it does total 1020.
- 1020 > 918 → **yes**.

Caveat: the entry's own annotations are internally inconsistent — the "Chain" feature (PRO_0000094446) spans only residues 1–816, and all functional features (CBS domains, ATP-binding sites, variants, PDB-derived secondary structure) stop by ~816, while the stored sequence runs to 1020. The ~204 extra C-terminal residues are unannotated, so the true mature/canonical length may be 816 rather than 1020 (in which case the answer would flip).

**Q9H252** (KCNH6_HUMAN, voltage‑gated potassium channel Kv11.2) — the UniProtKB sequence is **1150 aa** (127,004 Da, sequence version 2, 2024‑07‑24), which is more than 1054.

I verified the length by counting the sequence string directly (1150), and the residue numbering is internally consistent (e.g. N‑glycosylation site 449 = Asn, selectivity filter 476–481 = SVGFGN, variant 889 = Thr, conflict 927 = Phe).

Notable oddities:
- The annotated mature chain (PRO_0000054013) spans only residues 1–958, as does the final cytoplasmic topological domain, so ~192 C‑terminal residues of the stated 1150‑residue sequence lie outside the annotated chain.
- That C‑terminal extension (…ARRNERERNRVKLVNLGFATLREHVPNG…) is a classic bHLH transcription‑factor motif (NeuroD‑like), plus poly‑Ala/poly‑Gln tracts — consistent with a KCNH6–NEUROD2 read‑through/extended transcript rather than the channel itself. If one counts only the annotated channel chain, the length would be 958 (i.e. "no").

The INPP5K entry showed no such inconsistency.

Based on the sequence masses returned, **HORMAD1** (HORMA domain-containing protein 1, ~53.97 kDa) is heavier than INPP5K (inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase K, ~51.09 kDa) — a difference of only ~2.9 kDa.

Caveat worth noting: the HORMAD1 entry is internally inconsistent. Its canonical sequence is given as 473 aa, but the mature "Chain" feature is annotated as residues 1–394, and all other positional annotations (NLS motif at 383–386, last PDB β-strand at 387–390, disordered region ending at 394) stop at 394. A 394-residue chain would be roughly ~44–45 kDa, i.e. *lighter* than INPP5K — so the ranking flips depending on whether the full 473-aa record or the annotated chain is used. The INPP5K entry showed no such inconsistency.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.
Let me double-check the ETV4 record, since its stated sequence length (605) conflicts with its annotated chain (1–484).

**Results**

| Gene | Accession | Record length | Record mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| NETO1 | Q8TDF5 (isoform 3, displayed) | 533 aa | 60,191 Da ≈ **60.2 kDa** |
| ETV4 | P43268 | 605 aa (as returned) | 67,924 Da ≈ **67.9 kDa** |

**Important caveat:** the ETV4 record appears internally inconsistent/corrupted. Its own chain feature "ETS translocation variant 4" spans residues 1–484, all other features (DNA-binding ETS domain 341–421, PDB-derived secondary structure ending at 431, mutagenesis up to 443) stop well before residue 605, and the canonical Swiss-Prot ETV4 is 484 aa. The returned sequence carries ~121 extra C-terminal residues ("...RRLSRQSTRKEPVTKQVRLCVSPSGL...HCPSEFDD") that don't belong to any annotated ETV4 feature; the entry also lacks the crc64/md5 checksums that the NETO1 entry has. Removing those 121 residues (~13.6 kDa at this entry's mean residue mass) gives ~54 kDa for the annotated 1–484 chain, matching the published ETV4 mass (53,784 Da).

So: taken at face value the record would make ETV4 heavier (67.9 vs 60.2 kDa), but the biologically correct comparison is **NETO1 ≈ 60.2 kDa > ETV4 ≈ 54 kDa**, so NETO1 is the heavier protein.

**Results**

| Gene | Accession | Record length | Record mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| NETO1 | Q8TDF5 (isoform 3, displayed) | 533 aa | 60,191 Da ≈ **60.2 kDa** |
| ETV4 | P43268 | 605 aa (as returned) | 67,924 Da ≈ **67.9 kDa** |

**Important caveat:** the ETV4 record appears internally inconsistent/corrupted. Its own chain feature "ETS translocation variant 4" spans residues 1–484, all other features (DNA-binding ETS domain 341–421, PDB-derived secondary structure ending at 431, mutagenesis up to 443) stop well before residue 605, and the canonical Swiss-Prot ETV4 is 484 aa. The returned sequence carries ~121 extra C-terminal residues ("...RRLSRQSTRKEPVTKQVRLCVSPSGL...HCPSEFDD") that don't belong to any annotated ETV4 feature; the entry also lacks the crc64/md5 checksums that the NETO1 entry has. Removing those 121 residues (~13.6 kDa at this entry's mean residue mass) gives ~54 kDa for the annotated 1–484 chain, matching the published ETV4 mass (53,784 Da).

So: taken at face value the record would make ETV4 heavier (67.9 vs 60.2 kDa), but the biologically correct comparison is **NETO1 ≈ 60.2 kDa > ETV4 ≈ 54 kDa**, so NETO1 is the heavier protein.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**OR10J5** (Q8NHC4) — 371 aa, **41.55 kDa**
**HMX1** (Q9NP08) — 348 aa, **36.16 kDa**

OR10J5 is the heavier of the two, by about 5.4 kDa.

Note: the OR10J5 entry is a bit odd — the sequence is 371 aa but the annotated mature chain spans only residues 1–309, and the C-terminal ~60 residues look like an unrelated EF-hand/calmodulin-like stretch rather than a typical ~310-aa olfactory receptor. The 41.55 kDa figure is for the full 371-aa sequence; the 1–309 chain alone would be roughly 35 kDa, which would make HMX1 the heavier protein under that interpretation.

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by KCNQ3 or ZC3H3? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text:
## Comparison

**KCNQ3 → O43525 (KCNQ3_HUMAN)** — "Potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily KQT member 3"
- Sequence block in the record: 1090 aa, molWeight **121,613 Da (121.6 kDa)**
- **But**: the annotated mature chain (PRO_0000054034) is residues **1–872**, and all topological/domain features stop at 872. The last ~218 residues of the returned sequence ("…VWVDLEMTGLDIEKDQIIEMACLITDSD…") look like an unrelated DEDDh-type exonuclease segment appended to the KCNQ3 sequence. A genuine 872-residue KCNQ3 corresponds to roughly **97 kDa**.

**ZC3H3 → Q8IXZ2 (ZC3H3_HUMAN)** — "Zinc finger CCCH domain-containing protein 3"
- 948 aa, molWeight **101,941 Da (101.9 kDa)**; chain 1–948 is fully consistent with the sequence length.

## Verdict

- Taking the record values at face value, KCNQ3 (121.6 kDa) > ZC3H3 (101.9 kDa).
- Taking the *annotated protein chain* (which is internally consistent and matches the known 872-aa Kv7.3, ~96.8 kDa), **ZC3H3 (101.9 kDa) is the heavier protein**, vs KCNQ3 ~96.8 kDa.

I go with **ZC3H3** as heavier, since the KCNQ3 sequence string in this record appears corrupted/chimeric relative to its own chain annotation.

## Comparison

**KCNQ3 → O43525 (KCNQ3_HUMAN)** — "Potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily KQT member 3"
- Sequence block in the record: 1090 aa, molWeight **121,613 Da (121.6 kDa)**
- **But**: the annotated mature chain (PRO_0000054034) is residues **1–872**, and all topological/domain features stop at 872. The last ~218 residues of the returned sequence ("…VWVDLEMTGLDIEKDQIIEMACLITDSD…") look like an unrelated DEDDh-type exonuclease segment appended to the KCNQ3 sequence. A genuine 872-residue KCNQ3 corresponds to roughly **97 kDa**.

**ZC3H3 → Q8IXZ2 (ZC3H3_HUMAN)** — "Zinc finger CCCH domain-containing protein 3"
- 948 aa, molWeight **101,941 Da (101.9 kDa)**; chain 1–948 is fully consistent with the sequence length.

## Verdict

- Taking the record values at face value, KCNQ3 (121.6 kDa) > ZC3H3 (101.9 kDa).
- Taking the *annotated protein chain* (which is internally consistent and matches the known 872-aa Kv7.3, ~96.8 kDa), **ZC3H3 (101.9 kDa) is the heavier protein**, vs KCNQ3 ~96.8 kDa.

I go with **ZC3H3** as heavier, since the KCNQ3 sequence string in this record appears corrupted/chimeric relative to its own chain annotation.

**P50213 (IDH3A_HUMAN, isocitrate dehydrogenase [NAD] subunit alpha, mitochondrial)**

- Sequence length reported in the record: **458 residues** (I also counted the sequence string manually: 458; molecular weight 50,257 Da is consistent with that length).
- 458 > 412 → **yes**.

Caveat: the record is internally inconsistent in a notable way — the mature chain feature (PRO_0000014436) is annotated as residues 28–366, the disease-variant and secondary-structure features all stop at/before residue 366, and the C-terminal ~92 residues (from ~"QYQRAALQAK…" onward) carry no annotation at all. The canonical UniProt entry for P50213 is 366 aa (~39.6 kDa), so the 458-residue sequence here looks like it has an appended, unannotated extension.

- Sequence length reported in the record: **458 residues** (I also counted the sequence string manually: 458; molecular weight 50,257 Da is consistent with that length).
- 458 > 412 → **yes**.

Caveat: the record is internally inconsistent in a notable way — the mature chain feature (PRO_0000014436) is annotated as residues 28–366, the disease-variant and secondary-structure features all stop at/before residue 366, and the C-terminal ~92 residues (from ~"QYQRAALQAK…" onward) carry no annotation at all. The canonical UniProt entry for P50213 is 366 aa (~39.6 kDa), so the 458-residue sequence here looks like it has an appended, unannotated extension.

As recorded, **GPX1 (27.9 kDa) is heavier than COA7 (25.7 kDa)**, by ~2.2 kDa.

Important caveat: the GPX1 record is internally inconsistent — its annotated chain "Glutathione peroxidase 1" spans residues 1–203, yet the stored sequence is 254 aa (the canonical human GPX1 is normally 203 aa, ~22.1 kDa). If only the annotated 1–203 chain is counted (~22 kDa), COA7 would actually be the heavier protein. Also note COA7's mature chain is 2–231 (initiator Met removed, N-acetylated), making its mature mass slightly lower than 25.7 kDa.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**AHCYL2** — UniProt Q96HN2 (S‑adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase‑like protein 2)
- 611 aa, molecular weight 66,721 Da ≈ **66.7 kDa** (internally consistent: chain 2–611, no anomalies)

**ZNF835** — UniProt Q9Y2P0 (Zinc finger protein 835)
- The record's sequence is 671 aa / 74,502 Da ≈ 74.5 kDa, **but this record looks corrupted**:
  - The annotated chain ("Zinc finger protein 835") is **residues 1–537**, and all other features (14 C2H2 fingers, disordered region 497–537, compositional bias 509–524) stop at 537.
  - Residues ~538–671 are not zinc‑finger‑like at all; they contain the classic olfactory‑receptor/class‑A GPCR motifs ("…TAMGYDRYVAICRPLRY…", "…FFCDIYPVMK…"), i.e. an unrelated GPCR fragment appears to be appended.
- Mass of the genuine 537‑residue chain is therefore ≈ **59.5 kDa** (74.5 kDa minus the ~15 kDa spurious tail).

**Conclusion:** Taking the annotated ZNF835 chain (1–537, ~59.5 kDa), **AHCYL2 (66.7 kDa) is the heavier protein**. Note that if one naively uses the stored 671‑aa sequence mass (74.5 kDa), ZNF835 would appear heavier — but that value rests on an apparently chimeric sequence.

**Analysis of P49279 (NRAM1_HUMAN, SLC11A1)**

- The record's `sequence.length` field says **660**, and I counted the actual sequence string provided — it is indeed 660 residues (ends `...DQSDEESMNIVLQHIDFAIQ`).
- 660 > 605, so by the sequence in the record the answer is **yes**.

However, the record is internally inconsistent: the mature "Chain" feature is annotated 1–550, the last topological domain is 520–550 (cytoplasmic), and the last natural variant (D543N) and sequence conflict (544) all stop at 550 — consistent with the known canonical human SLC11A1 of 550 aa. The ~110 C‑terminal residues after position 550 are unannotated and look appended; if the true length were 550, the answer would be "no".

**Q92900 (UPF1_HUMAN, Regulator of nonsense transcripts 1)**

- Sequence length in the returned record: **1355 residues** (molWeight 149,326 Da) → 1355 > 1242, so **yes**.

Important caveat: the record is internally inconsistent. The annotated mature chain ("Regulator of nonsense transcripts 1", PRO_0000080716) spans residues **1–1129**, and all annotated features (domains, phospho-sites up to Ser-1127, mutagenesis, SQ domain 925–1129) stop at 1129 — consistent with the known UPF1 length (~1129 aa). The extra ~226 C-terminal residues in the sequence string (starting around "…CLKHTLATVPCDGCSYAKYCSQECLQQ…", which looks like an unrelated zinc-finger/MYND-like segment) are not covered by any annotation and appear spurious. If the true chain length (1129) is used, the answer would be "no".

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by HLX or ASB4? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Results**

| Gene | UniProt | Sequence in record | Reported molWeight |
|---|---|---|---|
| HLX | Q14774 (H2.0-like homeobox protein) | 488 aa, chain 1–488 | 50,789 Da ≈ **50.8 kDa** |
| ASB4 | Q9Y574 (Ankyrin repeat and SOCS box protein 4) | 511 aa listed, but chain annotated 1–**426** | 57,381 Da ≈ 57.4 kDa (for the 511‑aa string) |

**Problem with the ASB4 record:** the `sequence` field is 511 residues long, yet the only chain feature ("Ankyrin repeat and SOCS box protein 4") spans residues 1–426, and the isoform‑2 alternative‑sequence feature replaces residues 328–**426** ending exactly at "...LLLEPEGIIY" — the point where the extra 85 residues ("PIMLGKQLEGIWHTSIVVHKDE...FEHNCNT") begin. Those 85 C‑terminal residues appear to be spurious/appended. The 426‑residue annotated chain corresponds to roughly 47.8 kDa (consistent with 57.4 kDa minus ~9.5 kDa for the 85 extra residues).

**Conclusion:** Taking the ASB4 chain annotation (1–426, ~47.8 kDa) as the real protein, **HLX (~50.8 kDa) is heavier than ASB4 (~47.8 kDa)**. Note that if one instead trusted the inflated 511‑aa sequence/molWeight (57.4 kDa), ASB4 would appear heavier — so this answer hinges on the flagged inconsistency.

{"answer": "HLX", "concerns": ["ASB4 (Q9Y574) record is internally inconsistent: sequence field is 511 aa with molWeight 57,381 Da, but the chain feature spans only residues 1-426 and the isoform-2 alternative sequence ends at residue 426; the final 85 residues appear to be erroneously appended", "Because of this, ASB4's true mass is ~47.8 kDa (426 aa), not 57.4 kDa; using the uncorrected molWeight would flip the answer to ASB4", "HLX entry itself looks fine (488 aa, 50,789 Da, chain 1-488)"]}

| Gene | UniProt | Sequence in record | Reported molWeight |
|---|---|---|---|
| HLX | Q14774 (H2.0-like homeobox protein) | 488 aa, chain 1–488 | 50,789 Da ≈ **50.8 kDa** |
| ASB4 | Q9Y574 (Ankyrin repeat and SOCS box protein 4) | 511 aa listed, but chain annotated 1–**426** | 57,381 Da ≈ 57.4 kDa (for the 511‑aa string) |

**Problem with the ASB4 record:** the `sequence` field is 511 residues long, yet the only chain feature ("Ankyrin repeat and SOCS box protein 4") spans residues 1–426, and the isoform‑2 alternative‑sequence feature replaces residues 328–**426** ending exactly at "...LLLEPEGIIY" — the point where the extra 85 residues ("PIMLGKQLEGIWHTSIVVHKDE...FEHNCNT") begin. Those 85 C‑terminal residues appear to be spurious/appended. The 426‑residue annotated chain corresponds to roughly 47.8 kDa (consistent with 57.4 kDa minus ~9.5 kDa for the 85 extra residues).

**Conclusion:** Taking the ASB4 chain annotation (1–426, ~47.8 kDa) as the real protein, **HLX (~50.8 kDa) is heavier than ASB4 (~47.8 kDa)**. Note that if one instead trusted the inflated 511‑aa sequence/molWeight (57.4 kDa), ASB4 would appear heavier — so this answer hinges on the flagged inconsistency.

## Results

**COLEC11 — Q9BWP8 (Collectin‑11, CL‑K1)**
- 271 aa precursor, molecular weight **28,665 Da ≈ 28.7 kDa**
- Record is internally consistent (signal peptide 1–25, chain 26–271).

**NRL — P54845 (Neural retina‑specific leucine zipper protein)**
- The record reports length 284 aa, **molWeight 31,120 Da ≈ 31.1 kDa**
- **But this looks wrong:** the annotated chain "Neural retina‑specific leucine zipper protein" spans residues **1–237**, and *every* feature (bZIP domain 159–222, leucine zipper 187–208, all variants) stops at or before 237. The last ~47 residues of the stored sequence (`...GPGSGDPSHLFLYLIQHHIVHTGEKPYECSGCGKAFSFSSALIRHQRTHADSSGRLCPA`) are a classic **C2H2 zinc‑finger motif**, which does not belong to a bZIP factor — it appears to be a contaminating/chimeric C‑terminal extension. The mature NRL chain (1–237) would be roughly **25–26 kDa**.

**Comparison**
- Taking the records at face value: NRL (31.1 kDa) > COLEC11 (28.7 kDa).
- Using the biologically annotated NRL chain (1–237, ~25–26 kDa): **COLEC11 (28.7 kDa) is heavier**.

Because the NRL sequence/mass in this record is demonstrably inconsistent with its own feature annotation, I take the curated chain as authoritative: **COLEC11 encodes the heavier protein (~28.7 kDa vs ~25–26 kDa; 31.1 kDa as erroneously listed).**

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Lookups**

| Gene | Accession | Reported length | Reported mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANGPTL7 | O43827 (ANGL7_HUMAN), precursor, 346 aa | 346 aa | 40,018 Da ≈ **40.0 kDa** |
| HNRNPC | P07910 (HNRPC_HUMAN), isoform C2 | 382 aa (record) | 42,161 Da ≈ 42.2 kDa (record) |

**Important caveat:** the HNRNPC record returned is internally inconsistent. Its annotated chain is residues 2–306, the last annotated modified residue (phosphoserine) is at position 306, and the sequence conflict "EDDS" maps to 303–306 — i.e. the real canonical isoform C2 is 306 aa (~33.7 kDa). The returned sequence carries ~76 extra C‑terminal residues ("PANSVTKVSIQFERALLKWTEYTPDPNHGFYVSPSVLSALVPSMVAAKPVDWEESPLFNSLFPVSDGSNYFVRLYT") that are not covered by any feature annotation, inflating the stated mass to 42.2 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Using the properly annotated HNRNPC chain (306 aa, ~33.7 kDa), **ANGPTL7 (~40.0 kDa) is the heavier protein**. Only if one takes the (apparently corrupted) 382-aa/42.2 kDa entry at face value would HNRNPC appear heavier.

trace.system_prompt: You are a bioinformatics assistant. Use the provided tools to answer. End your reply with exactly one line of JSON: {"answer": ..., "concerns": [...]} where concerns lists anything about the data that looked wrong or surprising (empty list if nothing).
trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by DPH1 or DDI2? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**DDI2 is heavier.**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| DPH1 | Q9BZG8 (2-(3-amino-3-carboxypropyl)histidine synthase subunit 1) | 438 aa | 48,134 Da ≈ **48.1 kDa** |
| DDI2 | Q5TDH0 (Protein DDI1 homolog 2) | 479 aa | 53,053 Da ≈ **53.1 kDa** |

Difference: ~4.9 kDa in favour of DDI2.

Note: in the DDI2 entry the annotated mature chain spans residues 1–399 while the canonical sequence is 479 aa, so the chain feature appears inconsistent with the displayed sequence/mass. DPH1's displayed canonical isoform is isoform 4 (438 aa); other isoforms differ slightly in length, but all remain well below DDI2's mass.

Inflammasomes are supramolecular complexes that assemble in the cytosol in response to pathogens and other damage-associated signals and play critical roles in innate immunity and inflammation (PubMed:30674671). Acts as a recognition receptor (PRR): recognizes and binds specific pathogens and other damage-associated signals, such as lipoteichoic acid (LTA), a cell-wall component of Gram-positive bacteria, or double stranded RNA (dsRNA) (PubMed:30392956, PubMed:33377178, PubMed:34678144). May also recognize and bind lipopolysaccharide (LPS), a major component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria; however, LPS is probably not a major activator of the NLRP6 inflammasome (PubMed:31932628, PubMed:34678144). Following LTA- or dsRNA-binding, NLRP6 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), enhancing multivalent interactions, an essential step for the formation of the NLRP6 inflammasome polymeric complex (PubMed:34678144). The NLRP6 inflammasome acts by promoting recruitment of effector pro-inflammatory caspases (CASP1 and/or CASP4) that catalyze maturation and secretion of IL1B and IL18 in the extracellular milieu (PubMed:12387869, PubMed:30392956, PubMed:30674671, PubMed:34678144). The NLRP6 inflammasome plays a central role in the maintenance of epithelial integrity and host defense against microbial infections in the intestine (PubMed:30392956). Required to restrict infection against Gram-positive bacteria by recognizing lipoteichoic acid (LTA), leading to recruitment of CASP4 and CASP1, and subsequent maturation and secretion of IL1B and IL18 (PubMed:30392956, PubMed:33377178). Involved in intestinal antiviral innate immunity together with DHX15: recognizes and binds viral dsRNA to restrict infection by enteric viruses through the interferon pathway and GSDMD-dependent release of IL18 (PubMed:34161762, PubMed:34678144). Required to prevent infection by the apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium in enterocytes by promoting GSDMD-dependent release of IL18 (By similarity). The NLRP6 inflammasome may also regulate the gut microbiota composition by acting as a sensor of microbiota-associated metabolites to form a PYCARD/ASC-dependent inflammasome for downstream IL18 release and secretion of antimicrobial peptides (By similarity). Essential for gut mucosal self-renewal and proliferation (By similarity). - Under the chain annotation (874 aa), the answer would instead be "no", so the yes/no verdict hinges entirely on which length is trusted.

- The `sequence.length` field returned is **1205** residues (molWeight 136,769), so by the record's stated length it is **more than 1104**.

However, the record is internally inconsistent, and this matters for a threshold set at 1104:

- The annotated **Chain feature "BLOC-2 complex member HPS3" spans residues 1–1004**, and the isoform‑2 alternative-sequence features also terminate at 1004 (`VSP_003879`: 891–1004). This is the canonical HPS3 length.
- The ~201 residues after position 1004 ("...MECLDGGELFSRIQ... AHRDVKPENLLY... DFGFAKE... TPCYTPYYVAPEV... DMWSLGVIMYILLCGYPPFY...") form an unmistakable **protein‑kinase catalytic domain**, which has no business being in HPS3 (a BLOC‑2 scaffold protein with no kinase activity, no kinase keywords, no ATP‑binding/active‑site features annotated). This looks like a foreign C‑terminal segment concatenated onto the sequence.

So: answered "yes" on the literal returned sequence (1205), but the biologically correct HPS3 length is almost certainly 1004, which would make the answer "no".

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Comparison

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LAG3** | P18627 (LAG3_HUMAN) | 525 aa | 57,449 Da ≈ **57.4 kDa** |
| **ANGPTL3** | Q9Y5C1 (ANGL3_HUMAN) | *record says* 575 aa / 66,826 Da | true canonical: 460 aa ≈ **53.6 kDa** |

**Important caveat:** the ANGPTL3 record returned by the tool has a sequence of 575 aa with a stated mass of 66,826 Da, but this looks corrupted. Every annotation in the entry (chain "Angiopoietin-related protein 3" = 17–460, fibrinogen C-terminal domain 237–455, last beta strand 441–453, last variant N418Y) stops at residue 460, and the trailing ~115 residues ("…GKIPILEVDGLTLHQSLAIARYLTKNTDLAGNTEMEQCHVDAIVDTLDDFMSCFPWAEKK…") are an obvious glutathione S-transferase fusion-tag sequence, not ANGPTL3. The entry even carries a SEQUENCE CAUTION flag about a contaminating sequence. The genuine canonical ANGPTL3 is 460 aa, ~53.6 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the correct 460-aa ANGPTL3 (~53.6 kDa), **LAG3 (57.4 kDa) is the heavier protein**. (If one naively trusted the 575-aa/66.8 kDa figure, ANGPTL3 would appear heavier — but that mass includes a non-ANGPTL3 GST tag.)

Proposed to play a role in the trafficking of energy substrates to either storage or oxidative tissues in response to food intake (By similarity). Has a stimulatory effect on plasma triglycerides (TG), which is achieved by suppressing plasma TG clearance via inhibition of LPL activity. The inhibition of LPL activity appears to be an indirect mechanism involving recruitment of proprotein convertases PCSK6 and FURIN to LPL leading to cleavage and dissociation of LPL from the cell surface; the function does not require ANGPTL3 proteolytic cleavage but seems to be mediated by the N-terminal domain, and is not inhibited by GPIHBP1 (PubMed:12097324, PubMed:19318355, PubMed:20581395). Can inhibit endothelial lipase, causing increased plasma levels of high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and phospholipids (PubMed:17110602, PubMed:19028676). Can bind to adipocytes to activate lipolysis, releasing free fatty acids and glycerol (PubMed:12565906). Suppresses LPL specifically in oxidative tissues which is required to route very low density lipoprotein (VLDL)-TG to white adipose tissue (WAT) for storage in response to food; the function may involve cooperation with circulating, liver-derived ANGPTL8 and ANGPTL4 expression in WAT (By similarity). Contributes to lower plasma levels of low density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol by a mechanism that is independent of the canonical pathway implicating APOE and LDLR. ## Comparison

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LAG3** | P18627 (LAG3_HUMAN) | 525 aa | 57,449 Da ≈ **57.4 kDa** |
| **ANGPTL3** | Q9Y5C1 (ANGL3_HUMAN) | *record says* 575 aa / 66,826 Da | true canonical: 460 aa ≈ **53.6 kDa** |

**Important caveat:** the ANGPTL3 record returned by the tool has a sequence of 575 aa with a stated mass of 66,826 Da, but this looks corrupted. Every annotation in the entry (chain "Angiopoietin-related protein 3" = 17–460, fibrinogen C-terminal domain 237–455, last beta strand 441–453, last variant N418Y) stops at residue 460, and the trailing ~115 residues ("…GKIPILEVDGLTLHQSLAIARYLTKNTDLAGNTEMEQCHVDAIVDTLDDFMSCFPWAEKK…") are an obvious glutathione S-transferase fusion-tag sequence, not ANGPTL3. The entry even carries a SEQUENCE CAUTION flag about a contaminating sequence. The genuine canonical ANGPTL3 is 460 aa, ~53.6 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the correct 460-aa ANGPTL3 (~53.6 kDa), **LAG3 (57.4 kDa) is the heavier protein**. (If one naively trusted the 575-aa/66.8 kDa figure, ANGPTL3 would appear heavier — but that mass includes a non-ANGPTL3 GST tag.)

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**CLIC2 — O15247 (CLIC2_HUMAN)**
- Chloride intracellular channel protein 2
- 247 aa, molWeight = 28,356 Da ≈ **28.4 kDa** (chain 1–247 = full sequence)

**GOSR2 — O14653 (GOSR2_HUMAN)**
- Golgi SNAP receptor complex member 2 (membrin / "27 kDa Golgi SNARE protein")
- Record lists 265 aa, molWeight = 30,552 Da ≈ **30.6 kDa**
- **But** the annotated mature chain (PRO_0000212549) is only residues **1–212**, with the transmembrane anchor at 191–211 and the "vesicular" topological domain at residue 212 — i.e. the protein ends at 212. The extra 53 C‑terminal residues in the stored sequence (`HCVGDTYPSNDRCCHECRPGNGMVSRCSRSQNTVCRPCGPGFYNDVVSSKPC…`) are a cysteine‑rich, TNF‑receptor‑like stretch covered by no feature and inconsistent with the "27 kDa" alias and with the isoform 3 / isoform B alternative-sequence features (both of which also end at 212). That segment contributes ~5.9 kDa; the annotated 1–212 chain is ~24.7 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the record's listed sequence masses at face value, GOSR2 (30.6 kDa) > CLIC2 (28.4 kDa). However, the GOSR2 sequence in this record appears contaminated with a spurious 53‑residue C‑terminal extension; the genuine GOSR2 protein (212 aa, ≈24.7 kDa) is **lighter** than CLIC2 (28.4 kDa). I therefore report **CLIC2** as the heavier protein.

## Results

**CLIC2 — O15247 (CLIC2_HUMAN)**
- Chloride intracellular channel protein 2
- 247 aa, molWeight = 28,356 Da ≈ **28.4 kDa** (chain 1–247 = full sequence)

**GOSR2 — O14653 (GOSR2_HUMAN)**
- Golgi SNAP receptor complex member 2 (membrin / "27 kDa Golgi SNARE protein")
- Record lists 265 aa, molWeight = 30,552 Da ≈ **30.6 kDa**
- **But** the annotated mature chain (PRO_0000212549) is only residues **1–212**, with the transmembrane anchor at 191–211 and the "vesicular" topological domain at residue 212 — i.e. the protein ends at 212. The extra 53 C‑terminal residues in the stored sequence (`HCVGDTYPSNDRCCHECRPGNGMVSRCSRSQNTVCRPCGPGFYNDVVSSKPC…`) are a cysteine‑rich, TNF‑receptor‑like stretch covered by no feature and inconsistent with the "27 kDa" alias and with the isoform 3 / isoform B alternative-sequence features (both of which also end at 212). That segment contributes ~5.9 kDa; the annotated 1–212 chain is ~24.7 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the record's listed sequence masses at face value, GOSR2 (30.6 kDa) > CLIC2 (28.4 kDa). | Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass (record) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DPH1 | Q9BZG8 (DPH1_HUMAN, 2‑(3‑amino‑3‑carboxypropyl)histidine synthase subunit 1) | 438 aa | 48,134 Da ≈ **48.1 kDa** |
| PALM | O75781 (PALM_HUMAN, paralemmin‑1) | 484 aa | 53,657 Da ≈ **53.7 kDa** |

Taking the masses as stored in the records, **PALM (paralemmin‑1, ~53.7 kDa) is heavier than DPH1 (~48.1 kDa)**, by about 5.5 kDa.

Caveat: the PALM record looks internally inconsistent — its chain feature ends at residue 384 with a propeptide at 385–387 (i.e. a 387‑residue precursor, ~42 kDa), yet the stored sequence is 484 residues, and the extra C‑terminal stretch resembles an inositol‑polyphosphate‑phosphatase–like segment rather than paralemmin. If the true canonical sequence is the 387‑aa precursor, DPH1 would instead be the heavier protein.

Taking the masses as stored in the records, **PALM (paralemmin‑1, ~53.7 kDa) is heavier than DPH1 (~48.1 kDa)**, by about 5.5 kDa.

Caveat: the PALM record looks internally inconsistent — its chain feature ends at residue 384 with a propeptide at 385–387 (i.e. a 387‑residue precursor, ~42 kDa), yet the stored sequence is 484 residues, and the extra C‑terminal stretch resembles an inositol‑polyphosphate‑phosphatase–like segment rather than paralemmin. If the true canonical sequence is the 387‑aa precursor, DPH1 would instead be the heavier protein.

content.text:
**Q9P2Y4 (ZN219_HUMAN, Zinc finger protein 219)** — the entry's sequence record reports a length of **866 residues** (mol. weight ~93,169 Da), which is more than 794.

Caveats worth noting:
- The annotated mature chain feature "Zinc finger protein 219" (PRO_0000047461) spans residues **1–722**, not 1–866, so the chain annotation and the stated sequence length disagree. If the 722-residue chain were taken as the protein length, the answer would be "no".
- The C-terminal extension (~residues 745–866) contains two clear WW-domain-like motifs ("WVEGITSEGYHYYYD…WEKP", "WVEGLSEDGFTYYYN…WEKP") that resemble TCERG1/CA150-type domains rather than a C2H2 zinc-finger protein tail, and no features (regions, modifications) are annotated beyond residue 722 — suggesting the sequence string may be extended/chimeric relative to the curated chain.

{"answer": "yes", "concerns": ["Sequence length field says 866 aa but the annotated chain (PRO_0000047461) is only residues 1-722; these disagree and straddle the 794 threshold", "No sequence features of any type are annotated beyond residue 722", "The C-terminal ~120 residues contain two WW-domain-like motifs (GYHYYYD...WEKP / GFTYYYN...WEKP) atypical for a Krueppel C2H2 zinc-finger protein, suggesting a possibly erroneous/chimeric sequence extension"]}

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Protein | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RCVRN | P35243 | Recoverin | 200 aa | 23,130 Da ≈ **23.1 kDa** |
| GET1 (WRB/CHD5) | O00258 | Guided entry of tail-anchored proteins factor 1 | 218 aa | 24,882 Da ≈ **24.9 kDa** |

**GET1 is the heavier protein** (~24.9 kDa vs ~23.1 kDa for recoverin), a difference of ~1.75 kDa.

Caveats: GET1's annotated mature "Chain" feature is listed as residues 1–174 even though the canonical sequence is 218 aa — an internally inconsistent annotation; if only residues 1–174 were counted, GET1 would be the lighter of the two. Also, recoverin's mature chain is residues 2–200 (initiator Met removed) and is N-myristoylated, so its in-vivo mass differs slightly from the listed sequence mass; the comparison above uses the canonical full-sequence masses for both.

content.text:
**Q8TD43 — TRPM4_HUMAN** (Transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily M member 4, *Homo sapiens*)

- Sequence length reported in the record: **1518 residues** (molWeight 166,376 Da, consistent with ~1518 aa).
- 1518 > 1366 → **yes**.

Caveat: the record is internally inconsistent. The annotated mature chain is "1–1214" (PRO_0000259529), the last cytoplasmic topological domain ends at 1214, and a sequence conflict is annotated at position 1214 (D→E) — yet the stored sequence is 1518 aa and ends in ...VQVTTHRLCRL (not D). All features stop by residue 1214, suggesting ~300 extra C-terminal residues relative to the canonical isoform 1 length. If the canonical 1214-aa chain were used, the answer would instead be "no".

**Q8TD43 — TRPM4_HUMAN** (Transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily M member 4, *Homo sapiens*)

- Sequence length reported in the record: **1518 residues** (molWeight 166,376 Da, consistent with ~1518 aa).
- 1518 > 1366 → **yes**.

Caveat: the record is internally inconsistent. The annotated mature chain is "1–1214" (PRO_0000259529), the last cytoplasmic topological domain ends at 1214, and a sequence conflict is annotated at position 1214 (D→E) — yet the stored sequence is 1518 aa and ends in ...VQVTTHRLCRL (not D). All features stop by residue 1214, suggesting ~300 extra C-terminal residues relative to the canonical isoform 1 length. If the canonical 1214-aa chain were used, the answer would instead be "no".

## Comparison

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass (as reported) |
|---|---|---|---|
| RCVRN (recoverin) | P35243 | 240 aa (record) | 27.71 kDa |
| GOSR2 (membrin) | O14653 | 212 aa | 24.78 kDa |

**Important caveat:** the RCVRN record returned looks corrupted. Its annotations all describe a 200‑residue protein (chain "Recoverin" = residues 2–200, EF‑hands 1–4 ending at 182, last helix at 186, GRK1 site at 192), yet the stored sequence is 240 aa, with a 40‑residue C‑terminal tail ("...SQQSTINLSHNPLDCTCSNIHFLTWYKENLHKLEGS") that resembles a leucine‑rich‑repeat/LRR fragment and is unrelated to the recoverin family. Those extra ~40 residues account for ~4.4 kDa; the genuine recoverin chain (1–200) is ~23.2–23.3 kDa.

- Taking the record's stated mass at face value: RCVRN (27.71 kDa) > GOSR2 (24.78 kDa).
- Using the annotated/real recoverin chain (~23.3 kDa): **GOSR2 (24.78 kDa) is the heavier protein.**

I go with the biologically correct comparison: **GOSR2 ≈ 24.8 kDa vs RCVRN ≈ 23.3 kDa (27.7 kDa as erroneously listed)**.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**ARHGAP27 — Q6ZUM4 (RHG27_HUMAN), "Rho GTPase-activating protein 27"**
- Canonical isoform 1: 889 aa, **98,396 Da ≈ 98.4 kDa**

**MPO — P05164 (PERM_HUMAN), "Myeloperoxidase" (precursor)**
- The record returned a sequence of 931 aa with molWeight 104,816 Da (≈104.8 kDa), **but this record looks corrupted** (see concerns).
- All of the entry's own chain/feature annotations end at residue 745 (signal 1–48; "89 kDa MPO" 49–745; mature MPO 165–745; glycosylation/disulfides all ≤745), i.e. the genuine MPO precursor is 745 aa ≈ **83.9 kDa**, consistent with the entry's own naming of the "84 kDa"/"89 kDa" forms.

**Conclusion:** Taking MPO's real precursor (745 aa, ~84 kDa), **ARHGAP27 (~98.4 kDa) is the heavier protein** vs MPO (~83.9 kDa). Note that if one naively used the (apparently erroneous) 104.8 kDa value returned, MPO would appear heavier — so this comparison is sensitive to the data problem below.

"PubMed", "id": "9922160"}], "value": "Peroxidase that plays a central role in the host defense system of polymorphonuclear leukocytes by mediating both (1) formation of neutrophil extracellular trap (NETs) and (2) microbicidal activity (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:20974672, PubMed:20974816, PubMed:22131345, PubMed:25066128, PubMed:28574339, PubMed:40963017, PubMed:4978299, PubMed:6295491). Promotes NET formation by mediating chromatin disassembly: translocates to the nucleus and specifically binds to nucleosomes, both as monomer and homodimer, leading to nucleosome unstacking and initial chromatin decondensation (PubMed:40963017). Homodimers clash with one end of the nucleosomal DNA, leading to DNA unwrapping, initiating complete disassembly of nucleosomes and chromatin transformation into NETs in an ATP-independent manner (PubMed:40963017). NETs, which are mainly composed of DNA fibers and globular proteins, are then extruded into the extracellular space by neutrophils to trap pathogens and release antimicrobial proteins to destroy them (PubMed:40963017). Participates to the microbicidal activity against a wide range of organisms by acting as a peroxidase that catalyzes the formation of oxidants in presence of hydrogen peroxide (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17074761, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:21880720, PubMed:22131345, PubMed:22352991, PubMed:22902565, PubMed:24194519, PubMed:33273015, PubMed:9359420, PubMed:9922160). Mediates the formation of hypohalous acids, mainly hypochlorous acid (HOCl) in physiologic situations, that greatly enhance polymorphonuclear leukocyte microbicidal activity (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17074761, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:19608745, PubMed:21880720, PubMed:22902565, PubMed:24194519, PubMed:9359420, PubMed:9922160). In addition to hypochlorous acid, catalyzes formation of hypobromous acid (HOBr), hypoiodous acid (HOI) and hypothiocyanous acid (HOSCN) (PubMed:1318692, PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:19608745, PubMed:6295491, PubMed:9359420). Also catalyzes oxidation of nitrite into the highly reactive nitrogen dioxide radical (PubMed:10777476, PubMed:8385644, PubMed:9450756). Formation of oxidants are widely believed to be responsible for much of the anti-bactericidal activity of neutrophils (PubMed:8385644, PubMed:9450756). Oxidants, such as hypochlorous acid or nitrogen dioxide radical, can also oxidize amino acid residues on proteins and generate chlorination and nitration post-translational modifications, respectively (PubMed:15314690, PubMed:15326314, PubMed:15498770, PubMed:15574409, PubMed:16091367, PubMed:7622459). Chlorination and nitration of the lipid-free form of APOA1 impairs cholesterol transport (PubMed:15326314, PubMed:15498770, PubMed:15574409). Superoxides generated by MPO can also promote dioxygenation of tryptophan residues on proteins (PubMed:16091367, PubMed:40081572). Also able to oxidize melatonin into N1-acetyl-N2-formyl-5-methoxykynuramine either in presence of hydrogen peroxide or superoxide (PubMed:15636586, PubMed:16148002). Oxidizes urate into 5-hydroxyisourate (PubMed:21266577). Functions as a nitric oxide (NO) oxidase during inflammation, by catalytically consuming NO, impairing NO's ability to maintain vascular tone and function (PubMed:12089442). May also mediate the proteolytic cleavage of alpha-1-microglobulin to form t-alpha-1-microglobulin, which potently inhibits oxidation of low-density lipoprotein particles and limits vascular damage ## Results

**ARHGAP27 — Q6ZUM4 (RHG27_HUMAN), "Rho GTPase-activating protein 27"**
- Canonical isoform 1: 889 aa, **98,396 Da ≈ 98.4 kDa**

**MPO — P05164 (PERM_HUMAN), "Myeloperoxidase" (precursor)**
- The record returned a sequence of 931 aa with molWeight 104,816 Da (≈104.8 kDa), **but this record looks corrupted** (see concerns).
- All of the entry's own chain/feature annotations end at residue 745 (signal 1–48; "89 kDa MPO" 49–745; mature MPO 165–745; glycosylation/disulfides all ≤745), i.e. the genuine MPO precursor is 745 aa ≈ **83.9 kDa**, consistent with the entry's own naming of the "84 kDa"/"89 kDa" forms.

**Conclusion:** Taking MPO's real precursor (745 aa, ~84 kDa), **ARHGAP27 (~98.4 kDa) is the heavier protein** vs MPO (~83.9 kDa). Note that if one naively used the (apparently erroneous) 104.8 kDa value returned, MPO would appear heavier — so this comparison is sensitive to the data problem below.

content.text:
I retrieved the UniProtKB entry for Q8N4A0 (GALNT4_HUMAN, polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 4).

- The record's `sequence.length` field reports **694** residues (molWeight 79,171), so by that figure it exceeds 636.
- However, this looks inconsistent with the rest of the entry: the annotated chain PRO_0000059108 spans residues 1–578, the lumenal topological domain ends at 578, the ricin B-type lectin domain ends at 577, and no feature (binding site, disulfide, strand/helix) extends beyond 578. The published length for GALNT4 is 578 aa.
- The extra C-terminal stretch (…LDCEMVGVGPKGEESMAARVSIVNQYGK…KGRILV, ~116 residues) contains a DEDDh-type exonuclease motif unrelated to GalNAc-transferases, suggesting a sequence concatenation/contamination in this record.

If the true mature chain (578 aa) is used, the answer would be "no"; based on the stored sequence field, it is "yes".

I retrieved the UniProtKB entry for Q8N4A0 (GALNT4_HUMAN, polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 4).

- The record's `sequence.length` field reports **694** residues (molWeight 79,171), so by that figure it exceeds 636.
- However, this looks inconsistent with the rest of the entry: the annotated chain PRO_0000059108 spans residues 1–578, the lumenal topological domain ends at 578, the ricin B-type lectin domain ends at 577, and no feature (binding site, disulfide, strand/helix) extends beyond 578. The published length for GALNT4 is 578 aa.
- The extra C-terminal stretch (…LDCEMVGVGPKGEESMAARVSIVNQYGK…KGRILV, ~116 residues) contains a DEDDh-type exonuclease motif unrelated to GalNAc-transferases, suggesting a sequence concatenation/contamination in this record.

If the true mature chain (578 aa) is used, the answer would be "no"; based on the stored sequence field, it is "yes".

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by ELL2 or AHCYL2? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Lookups**

| Gene | Accession / Entry | Annotated length | Annotated mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ELL2 | O00472 (ELL2_HUMAN, RNA Pol II elongation factor ELL2) | 640 aa | 72,324 Da ≈ **72.3 kDa** |
| AHCYL2 | Q96HN2 (SAHH3_HUMAN, S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase-like protein 2 / long-IRBIT) | 764 aa listed | 83,666 Da ≈ 83.7 kDa (see caveat) |

**Caveat on the AHCYL2 record:** the entry is internally inconsistent. The mature chain feature (PRO_0000116909) runs only from residue 2 to **611**, and every other feature (binding sites, helices, alternative-sequence isoforms) stops before residue 600 — yet the stored sequence is 764 aa. The extra C‑terminal ~153 residues ("…GGVDRHKQFWRYFAGNLASGGAAGATSLCFVYPLDFARTRL…PFDTVRRRMMMQS") are a classic mitochondrial solute-carrier (SLC25/ADP-ATP translocase) motif, unrelated to the adenosylhomocysteinase fold, i.e. an apparent concatenation artifact. The real AHCYL2 polypeptide (611 aa) corresponds to roughly 66–67 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the annotated AHCYL2 chain (2–611, ~67 kDa) as the genuine protein, **ELL2 (72.3 kDa) is heavier than AHCYL2 (~67 kDa; 83.7 kDa only if the apparently corrupted 764‑aa sequence is taken at face value)**.

**Lookups**

| Gene | Accession / Entry | Annotated length | Annotated mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ELL2 | O00472 (ELL2_HUMAN, RNA Pol II elongation factor ELL2) | 640 aa | 72,324 Da ≈ **72.3 kDa** |
| AHCYL2 | Q96HN2 (SAHH3_HUMAN, S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase-like protein 2 / long-IRBIT) | 764 aa listed | 83,666 Da ≈ 83.7 kDa (see caveat) |

**Caveat on the AHCYL2 record:** the entry is internally inconsistent. The mature chain feature (PRO_0000116909) runs only from residue 2 to **611**, and every other feature (binding sites, helices, alternative-sequence isoforms) stops before residue 600 — yet the stored sequence is 764 aa. The extra C‑terminal ~153 residues ("…GGVDRHKQFWRYFAGNLASGGAAGATSLCFVYPLDFARTRL…PFDTVRRRMMMQS") are a classic mitochondrial solute-carrier (SLC25/ADP-ATP translocase) motif, unrelated to the adenosylhomocysteinase fold, i.e. an apparent concatenation artifact. The real AHCYL2 polypeptide (611 aa) corresponds to roughly 66–67 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the annotated AHCYL2 chain (2–611, ~67 kDa) as the genuine protein, **ELL2 (72.3 kDa) is heavier than AHCYL2 (~67 kDa; 83.7 kDa only if the apparently corrupted 764‑aa sequence is taken at face value)**.
